title: Software architecture advice report — content specifications
source: The 23-section report outline in the current conversation.
purpose: Proposed report-content specifications; not a completed codebase analysis or independently validated customer research.

sections.title: Executive architecture brief
sections.purpose: Give decision-makers a concise, evidence-backed orientation and a short list of decisions that deserve attention.

specifications.title: What the system does
specifications.question: What business work does this system perform, for whom, and where does its responsibility end?

specifications.title: Overall architecture shape
specifications.question: How is the system organized, and which architectural choices define how it operates?

specifications.title: Major strengths and weaknesses
specifications.question: What should we preserve, and what currently obstructs our goals?

specifications.title: Top architectural risks
specifications.question: Which three to five architectural risks most deserve management attention?

specifications.title: Immediate versus later priorities
specifications.question: What should we address now, plan next, and deliberately leave alone?

sections.title: Inferred system architecture
sections.purpose: Reconstruct how the implementation actually works instead of mirroring the directory tree or repeating potentially stale diagrams.

specifications.title: Major subsystems and responsibilities
specifications.question: What are the main functional parts, and what work is each responsible for?

specifications.title: Service and module boundaries
specifications.question: Where are the actual separation points, and how strong are those boundaries?

specifications.title: Runtime and deployment topology
specifications.question: What runs where, and how do deployment and operational boundaries differ from source structure?

specifications.title: External dependencies
specifications.question: Which third-party or out-of-scope systems does this architecture rely on?

specifications.title: Critical request and data flows
specifications.question: How do important requests and data travel across the system?

specifications.title: How the system actually works
specifications.question: What operational story explains the implementation beyond its file layout?

sections.title: Natural boundaries versus current boundaries
sections.purpose: Identify where responsibility, data, and change patterns suggest better boundaries while preserving explicit tradeoffs.

specifications.title: Recommended component boundaries
specifications.question: Where would boundaries better match responsibilities and independent change?

specifications.title: Mixed responsibilities
specifications.question: Which components combine concerns that should change or be governed separately?

specifications.title: Merge candidates
specifications.question: Which separated components create overhead without meaningful independence?

specifications.title: Extraction and decomposition candidates
specifications.question: What can be separated safely, and what prevents separation today?

specifications.title: Domain boundary violations
specifications.question: Where does one domain reach into another domain’s rules or internal representation?

sections.title: Hidden coupling
sections.purpose: Expose dependencies that make apparently local changes require broader coordination or produce unexpected behavior.

specifications.title: Unexpected dependencies
specifications.question: Which components depend on one another in ways the architecture model does not explain?

specifications.title: Circular dependencies
specifications.question: Which components form dependency cycles, and how do those cycles constrain change?

specifications.title: Temporal and co-change coupling
specifications.question: Which components must be used in a particular order or repeatedly change together?

specifications.title: Shared-state coupling
specifications.question: Which components influence one another through state rather than explicit interfaces?

specifications.title: Implicit contracts
specifications.question: What unstated expectations must remain true for components to cooperate?

specifications.title: Cross-layer dependencies
specifications.question: Where does code cross or reverse an intended architectural layer boundary?

sections.title: Change blast-radius analysis
sections.purpose: For a specific proposed change, identify what may be affected, why, and how to validate the result.

specifications.title: Change scenario definition
specifications.question: Exactly what change are we evaluating, and what counts as an impact?

specifications.title: Direct dependents
specifications.question: Which immediate consumers need review for this change?

specifications.title: Transitive dependents
specifications.question: How could this change propagate beyond immediate consumers?

specifications.title: Affected APIs and contracts
specifications.question: Which public or internal contracts could change for consumers?

specifications.title: Data and schema dependencies
specifications.question: Which data consumers, migrations, and invariants are affected?

specifications.title: Tests to run
specifications.question: Which tests provide useful evidence that this change is safe?

specifications.title: Affected services and deployments
specifications.question: Which operational units must change, restart, or coordinate a release?

specifications.title: Historical co-change evidence
specifications.question: What past changes suggest additional review targets for this change?

sections.title: Architecture hotspots
sections.purpose: Identify components where structural difficulty, active change, operational importance, and weak validation combine to warrant attention.

specifications.title: Code complexity
specifications.question: Where is implementation complexity concentrated at an architectural level?

specifications.title: Git churn
specifications.question: Which architectural areas absorb the most change?

specifications.title: Dependency centrality
specifications.question: Which components occupy influential positions in the dependency structure?

specifications.title: Production criticality
specifications.question: Which components support the outcomes the customer can least afford to lose?

specifications.title: Bug-fix concentration
specifications.question: Where does corrective work repeatedly accumulate?

specifications.title: Test coverage gaps
specifications.question: Where do important architectural behaviors lack credible verification?

specifications.title: Prioritized hotspot map
specifications.question: Which components should receive architectural attention first, and why?

sections.title: Architecture debt and smells
sections.purpose: Turn structural symptoms into evidenced architectural findings, accounting for intentional tradeoffs and the cost of remediation.

specifications.title: God components
specifications.question: Which components accumulate excessive responsibilities or authority?

specifications.title: Dependency cycles as architectural debt
specifications.question: Which dependency cycles create enough ongoing cost to justify intervention?

specifications.title: Layer violations as architectural debt
specifications.question: Which layer-rule exceptions create a meaningful maintenance obligation?

specifications.title: Excessive centralization
specifications.question: Where does centralized control or state impose an avoidable system-wide constraint?

specifications.title: Leaky abstractions
specifications.question: Where must consumers understand details that an interface is meant to hide?

specifications.title: Duplicate mechanisms
specifications.question: Where do multiple implementations solve the same architectural problem inconsistently?

specifications.title: Ownership boundary mismatches
specifications.question: Where are architectural responsibilities assigned in ways that create unresolved control or coordination?

specifications.title: Fan-in and fan-out
specifications.question: Where do unusually broad dependency relationships create a practical design concern?

specifications.title: Architecture drift
specifications.question: Where has implementation moved away from an agreed or previously observed architecture?

sections.title: Data and state ownership
sections.purpose: Make ownership, access, durability, consistency, and failure behavior explicit for important data and operational state.

specifications.title: Data ownership
specifications.question: Who has authority over each important data entity and its rules?

specifications.title: Data writers
specifications.question: Which actors can create, update, or delete important state?

specifications.title: Data readers
specifications.question: Who depends on the meaning, shape, and freshness of this data?

specifications.title: Sources of truth
specifications.question: Which representation is authoritative when copies disagree?

specifications.title: Cache topology and invalidation
specifications.question: Where is data cached, and what keeps cached behavior acceptably correct?

specifications.title: Durable versus ephemeral state
specifications.question: What survives process loss, and what must be reconstructed?

specifications.title: Consistency and disagreement
specifications.question: Can components hold conflicting views, and how is disagreement resolved?

specifications.title: Partial-failure behavior of state
specifications.question: What happens when only part of a multi-step state change succeeds?

specifications.title: CRUD and ownership matrix
specifications.question: Can we see data authority and access patterns in one actionable view?

sections.title: Critical workflow analysis
sections.purpose: Explain important end-to-end behavior and the architectural constraints hidden within execution sequences.

specifications.title: End-to-end workflow
specifications.question: How does an important customer or operational task complete?

specifications.title: Critical workflow path
specifications.question: Which dependent steps determine when this workflow can complete?

specifications.title: Workflow failure points
specifications.question: Where can this workflow fail, and what does the customer observe?

specifications.title: Cross-boundary calls
specifications.question: Which workflow steps cross a boundary that adds coordination or operational obligations?

specifications.title: Workflow state transitions
specifications.question: What states can the work occupy, and which transitions are valid?

specifications.title: Retry and idempotency behavior
specifications.question: Can this workflow be retried without losing work or duplicating effects?

specifications.title: Hidden workflow dependencies
specifications.question: What must be true outside the explicit workflow graph for it to succeed?

sections.title: Reliability and failure architecture
sections.purpose: Assess how architectural boundaries, state, and recovery mechanisms behave under explicitly scoped failure scenarios.

specifications.title: Single points of failure
specifications.question: Which individual failures can prevent an important capability from operating?

specifications.title: Failure cascades
specifications.question: How can one local failure spread to otherwise healthy parts of the system?

specifications.title: Dependency unavailability
specifications.question: What happens when an important dependency is slow, unreachable, or returns errors?

specifications.title: State inconsistency risks
specifications.question: Which failures can leave the system believing mutually incompatible things?

specifications.title: Restart and retry behavior
specifications.question: Can interrupted work resume safely after a process or host restarts?

specifications.title: Recovery mechanism gaps
specifications.question: Where does the architecture lack a workable path back to a correct operating state?

sections.title: Scalability ceilings
sections.purpose: Identify plausible capacity limits under explicit workload assumptions and distinguish measured ceilings from unverified scaling hypotheses.

specifications.title: First limiting component
specifications.question: Under a defined growth scenario, which component is likely to constrain useful throughput first?

specifications.title: Bottleneck mechanisms
specifications.question: Why would a proposed bottleneck constrain the system?

specifications.title: Resource capacity constraints
specifications.question: Which CPU, memory, network, storage, database, or quota limits matter to growth?

specifications.title: Centralized bottlenecks
specifications.question: Which centralized operations can cap throughput or prevent independent scaling?

specifications.title: Shared resource contention
specifications.question: Where do workloads interfere because they compete for the same resources?

specifications.title: Tenfold and hundredfold growth scenarios
specifications.question: What would have to change at 10× or 100× a clearly defined workload?

sections.title: Performance and latency architecture
sections.purpose: Focus on structural sources of delay and resource work rather than unprioritized line-level micro-optimization.

specifications.title: Critical latency paths
specifications.question: Which architectural stages account for delay in important user or job outcomes?

specifications.title: Serial dependencies
specifications.question: Which sequential steps are necessary, and which could be overlapped or removed?

specifications.title: Excessive remote calls
specifications.question: Where does the architecture perform avoidable network interactions?

specifications.title: Chatty service boundaries
specifications.question: Do service contracts force repeated back-and-forth to complete one coherent task?

specifications.title: Data movement
specifications.question: Where does transporting, copying, or transforming data dominate architectural work?

specifications.title: Synchronization points
specifications.question: Where do locks, barriers, transactions, or coordination waits delay independent work?

sections.title: Security and trust boundaries
sections.purpose: Describe architectural security exposure and control boundaries without implying that an architecture review is a complete security audit.

specifications.title: Trust boundary map
specifications.question: Where does the system accept data or actions from an actor with a different trust level?

specifications.title: Privilege concentration
specifications.question: Which identities or components hold authority far broader than their normal responsibilities?

specifications.title: Sensitive-data flows
specifications.question: Where does sensitive information enter, move, persist, and leave the architecture?

specifications.title: Authentication and authorization boundaries
specifications.question: Where are identity and permission decisions made and enforced?

specifications.title: Dependency and security exposure
specifications.question: Which dependencies or architectural interfaces expand the security exposure under review?

specifications.title: Security blast radius
specifications.question: What could an attacker or unauthorized actor reach from a compromised architectural unit?

sections.title: Architecture evolution
sections.purpose: Compare meaningful architectural changes over time using compatible snapshots and clearly defined history windows.

specifications.title: Coupling trends
specifications.question: Are component dependencies becoming more or less constraining over time?

specifications.title: Hotspot growth
specifications.question: Which architectural hotspots are emerging, worsening, or improving?

specifications.title: Boundary deterioration
specifications.question: Which previously useful boundaries are losing their intended separation?

specifications.title: Responsibility accumulation
specifications.question: Which components are steadily acquiring unrelated roles?

specifications.title: Technical debt trends
specifications.question: Is the architecture’s unresolved maintenance burden increasing, decreasing, or changing form?

specifications.title: Architecture diff between releases
specifications.question: What changed architecturally between two specific releases?

sections.title: Team and architecture alignment
sections.purpose: Identify where technical boundaries and actual accountability support or obstruct coordinated delivery without evaluating individual employees.

specifications.title: Code ownership
specifications.question: Who maintains and reviews each important part of the implementation?

specifications.title: Team ownership
specifications.question: Which team is accountable for each capability, service, and operational outcome?

specifications.title: Team-to-service boundary alignment
specifications.question: Do technical units match the responsibilities teams can actually own independently?

specifications.title: Cross-team change patterns
specifications.question: Which kinds of changes repeatedly require coordination across teams?

specifications.title: Shared subsystem coordination
specifications.question: Where do several teams repeatedly contend for the same architectural decision or release?

sections.title: Decision and what-if analysis
sections.purpose: Evaluate concrete architectural changes as bounded scenarios, with dependencies, tradeoffs, and uncertainty made explicit.

specifications.title: Service split scenarios
specifications.question: What would happen if this service were split along a proposed seam?

specifications.title: Safe module extraction
specifications.question: Can this module be extracted without breaking its consumers or hidden obligations?

specifications.title: Technology replacement
specifications.question: What would replacing a database, queue, framework, or other platform actually affect?

specifications.title: Workload relocation
specifications.question: What changes if this work moves to another service, process, host, or environment?

specifications.title: Component elimination
specifications.question: What would break or need to move if we removed this component?

specifications.title: Microservice independence
specifications.question: In what ways is this microservice actually independent, and in what ways is it not?

sections.title: Alternative target architectures
sections.purpose: Offer comparable intervention options rather than a single prescriptive redesign, including the consequences of retaining the current architecture.

specifications.title: Minimal intervention option
specifications.question: What is the smallest change that reduces the immediate risk?

specifications.title: Boundary cleanup option
specifications.question: What targeted boundary work would improve maintainability without wholesale restructuring?

specifications.title: Architectural restructuring option
specifications.question: What broader redesign could address long-term structural requirements?

specifications.title: Option tradeoffs and selection
specifications.question: How do the options compare under the customer’s actual priorities and constraints?

sections.title: Concrete prioritized recommendations
sections.purpose: Convert findings into a short, traceable set of actions with impact, effort, priority, and verifiable outcomes.

specifications.title: Finding statement
specifications.question: What exactly is wrong or worth improving, and under what conditions?

specifications.title: Supporting evidence for a recommendation
specifications.question: What evidence supports this finding and the proposed response?

specifications.title: Impact assessment
specifications.question: Why does this finding matter to the customer?

specifications.title: Recommended action
specifications.question: What specific change or investigation should the customer undertake?

specifications.title: Effort estimate
specifications.question: What work and uncertainty determine the likely implementation effort?

specifications.title: Validation plan
specifications.question: How will we know the recommendation produced the intended improvement?

specifications.title: Priority and ordering
specifications.question: Which recommendations should be undertaken first, and what must precede them?

sections.title: Sequenced migration and refactoring roadmap
sections.purpose: Turn selected recommendations into a safe sequence with explicit dependencies, compatibility windows, validation gates, and rollback constraints.

specifications.title: Migration stages and milestones
specifications.question: How can the target architecture be reached through controlled intermediate states?

specifications.title: Contract establishment
specifications.question: What explicit contracts must exist before moving responsibilities?

specifications.title: State isolation
specifications.question: How will data and execution state be prepared for the new ownership boundary?

specifications.title: Read-path migration
specifications.question: How will readers move to the new interface or store without silent behavior changes?

specifications.title: Write-path migration
specifications.question: How will authority for state changes move without losing or duplicating effects?

specifications.title: Service extraction and cutover
specifications.question: How will the prepared boundary become an independently operated unit?

specifications.title: Recommendation dependencies and safe order
specifications.question: Which actions must precede others, and which can safely proceed in parallel?

specifications.title: Rollback and exit criteria
specifications.question: When should the migration stop, reverse, or be considered complete?

sections.title: Business impact
sections.purpose: Translate architectural mechanisms into decision-relevant outcomes, keeping measured results, estimates, and hypotheses separate.

specifications.title: Change lead time
specifications.question: How does the architecture influence the time needed to deliver a meaningful change?

specifications.title: Release risk
specifications.question: How does the architecture affect the chance or consequence of a problematic release?

specifications.title: Incident likelihood
specifications.question: What does the available evidence say about architectural contributors to incident risk?

specifications.title: Developer coordination cost
specifications.question: Which architectural dependencies create avoidable coordination work?

specifications.title: Infrastructure cost
specifications.question: Which architectural choices drive recurring infrastructure cost, and what could change it?

specifications.title: Scaling capability
specifications.question: What business growth can the architecture support, and what investment would unlock more?

specifications.title: Hiring and onboarding complexity
specifications.question: How does the architecture affect the effort required for a new contributor to become effective?

specifications.title: Independent deployment
specifications.question: How much release autonomy do teams or services actually have?

sections.title: Evidence and confidence
sections.purpose: Make every material claim auditable, scoped, and explicit about what is observed, inferred, assumed, or not known.

specifications.title: Source-code evidence
specifications.question: Can a reviewer locate the implementation that supports this claim?

specifications.title: Runtime trace evidence
specifications.question: What observed execution supports the architectural behavior or timing claim?

specifications.title: Dependency-edge evidence
specifications.question: What does each important edge mean, and where did it come from?

specifications.title: Historical commit evidence
specifications.question: Which actual changes support the report’s evolutionary claims?

specifications.title: Incident and test evidence
specifications.question: Which failures or checks demonstrate the claimed behavior?

specifications.title: Confidence assessment
specifications.question: How strongly does the available evidence support each material claim?

specifications.title: Counterevidence and uncertainty
specifications.question: What could make this finding or recommendation wrong?

specifications.title: Claim-to-evidence traceability
specifications.question: Can every conclusion, recommendation, and work package be traced back to verifiable observations?

sections.title: Unknowns and verification tasks
sections.purpose: Make analysis limits explicit and convert consequential uncertainty into concrete, bounded information-gathering work.

specifications.title: Undetermined findings
specifications.question: Which important questions could not be answered from the available evidence?

specifications.title: Missing runtime information
specifications.question: What operational evidence is needed to validate the static architecture model?

specifications.title: Assumptions register
specifications.question: Which unverified premises are influencing the report’s conclusions?

specifications.title: Next measurements and verification tasks
specifications.question: What should we check next to reduce the most consequential uncertainty?

sections.title: Implementation-ready work packages
sections.purpose: Express approved or proposed improvements as bounded tasks that a human engineer or coding agent can execute and verify under explicit authority.

specifications.title: Task goal
specifications.question: What single outcome should this work package deliver?

specifications.title: Relevant files and components
specifications.question: Where should the implementer look, and which adjacent areas could be affected?

specifications.title: Architectural constraints
specifications.question: What properties and boundaries must the implementation preserve?

specifications.title: Non-goals
specifications.question: What work should explicitly not be included in this task?

specifications.title: Migration steps within a work package
specifications.question: What sequence should the implementer follow to reach the task goal safely?

specifications.title: Required tests
specifications.question: What checks must accompany this work before it can be accepted?

specifications.title: Acceptance criteria
specifications.question: What objective evidence allows this task to be accepted?

specifications.title: Coding-agent handoff
specifications.question: Can a coding agent execute this bounded task without guessing the intent or its authority?
